title: CCST IT Support (100-140) practice exam

domains.name: IT Support Job Tasks and Responsibilities

note: Original questions written for MyNextCert from Cisco's public 100-140 CCST IT Support exam topic blueprint (form 4/24, checked 2026-11-23). Not real exam questions. Cisco doesn't publish the number of items or the topic weights, so this is a 45-item stand-in that fits the real 50 minutes, with an even split across the six domains and 4 drag-and-drop style items.

q.q: Forty tickets are waiting at 9 a.m. One is a password reset, one is a file-server outage that stops 200 people from working, and the rest are routine. Which one do you work first?
o: The one from the loudest caller
Volume isn't priority. Impact and urgency set the order.
Whichever came in first, to keep it fair
First-in, first-out ignores impact. A big outage costs more with every minute.
The password reset, since it takes two minutes
Quick wins feel good, but they don't help 200 blocked users.
The outage, because it hurts the most people
Right. Order the queue by impact and urgency, not by who asked first.

q.q: Your contract says every high-priority ticket must get a first reply within 15 minutes. What is that promise called?
o: A change request
A change request asks permission to alter a system.
An acceptable use policy
That policy tells users what they may do with company equipment.
A service level agreement (SLA)
Right. An SLA sets the response and fix times the help desk has agreed to.
A key performance indicator (KPI)
A KPI is a number you track, such as how often you meet the SLA.

q.q: A manager wants one number that shows how often tickets are solved without handing them to another team. Which KPI is that?
o: Number of user accounts
A head count says nothing about how well tickets are solved.
First-contact resolution rate
Right. It counts the tickets fixed on the first contact.
Mean time between failures
That rates how reliable hardware is.
Uptime percentage
Uptime measures how long a service stays available, not how tickets are handled.

q.q: Why does a help desk log every request in a ticketing system instead of working from phone calls and hallway chats?
o: It makes problems fix themselves once logged
Logging doesn't fix anything. People do.
It removes the need for an SLA
SLA timers are usually tracked inside the ticketing system.
Each request gets an owner and a history
Right. A ticket is the single record of who asked, who owns it and what was done.
It lets technicians skip writing notes
The ticket is only as useful as the notes you add to it.

q.q: You have spent two hours on one hard ticket. Four more are waiting, and one of them is about to break its SLA. What is the best move?
o: Note what you tried, then escalate or ask for help
Right. Escalate with notes so the next person doesn't start over, and get back to the queue.
Ignore the waiting tickets because this one was first
Order is set by priority and SLA time left, not by who got there first.
Keep going alone until it is solved
Stalling on one ticket lets the others breach their SLAs.
Close the ticket and tell the user to open a new one
Closing without a fix is dishonest and hides the problem in your numbers.

q.q: Which ticket note would help the next technician the most?
o: Fixed printer.
Too thin. The next tech can't see what was tried or what worked.
Printer offline. Checked power and cable, cleared the queue, reinstalled the driver. It prints now and the user confirmed.
Right. It gives the problem, the steps and the result.
User can't work a printer, my guess is it's their fault.
A guess about blame is opinion, not fact.
Did the usual steps. Works now.
'The usual steps' means nothing to someone who wasn't there.

q.q: A technician writes 'this user is clueless and breaks everything' in a ticket. What is wrong with that?
o: It is too short to be useful
Length isn't the issue. The content is.
Ticket notes must be factual and professional, because other people read them
Right. Notes can be read by users, managers and auditors. Stick to facts.
Nothing, because internal notes can hold opinions
Internal notes still get read, and opinions can cause real harm.
It should have been said in a chat message instead
Moving it to chat doesn't make it professional.

q.q: Which TWO items belong in a ticket's closing notes? (Choose two.)
o: Details of unrelated tickets
Each ticket should hold only its own facts.
The result, such as the user confirming it works
Right. The result shows the problem is really closed.
The cause, if known, and the fix that worked
Right. This is what lets the next tech solve it faster.
The user's password, so it's handy next time
Never store passwords in a ticket.
A guess about who is to blame
Blame is opinion and has no place in a ticket.

q.q: Why write down the steps that did NOT fix the problem?
o: Because every SLA needs at least ten steps
No SLA counts steps.
To make the ticket look like more work was done
Padding is dishonest. Notes should be true and useful.
So the user can see their mistakes
Notes are for the team, not for blaming the user.
It shows the next tech what's already ruled out
Right. Dead ends save the next tech time.

q.q: During a call the user reads out their password so you can 'log in as them'. What do you do with it when you write the ticket?
o: Ignore it, since the ticket is internal
Internal doesn't mean safe.
Write it in the ticket in case it's needed again
Tickets are read by many people. Passwords don't belong there.
Leave it out, and tell the user to change it
Right. A password in a ticket is a leak, and the user should treat it as exposed.
Put it in the private notes only
Private notes can still be seen by admins and in exports.

q.q: A user says 'the Wi-Fi is slow'. Which step of the process comes first?
o: Reboot the router
Rebooting is a guess without details.
Define the problem
Right. First make sure you understand the problem the way the user sees it.
Rebuild the laptop
A rebuild is a last resort, not a first step.
Replace the access point
That is a fix. You don't have a cause yet.

q.q: You changed a DNS setting and the website now loads. What comes next?
o: Confirm with the user, then document
Right. Check that it holds and the user agrees, then record the fix.
Close the ticket without checking
Always confirm with the user first.
Make a second change to be safe
Extra changes make it harder to know what worked.
Go back and gather information again
The problem is solved. Only repeat if it is not.

q.q: Your first fix didn't work. What does the process tell you to do?
o: Close it as 'cannot reproduce' right away
That should only come after real checks.
Tell the user nothing is wrong
The problem is still real.
Pick another likely cause, or escalate
Right. Loop back with new information, and ask for help if you're stuck.
Apply every possible fix at once
You'd never know which change worked, and might break more.

q.q: A user says 'my computer is broken'. Which follow-up best gathers detail?
o: Did you install something you shouldn't have?
That blames the user and puts them on the defensive.
Have you read the IT policy?
That doesn't help find the cause.
Can you just bring it to the help desk?
That jumps to a solution before you know the problem.
What happens, since when, and what changed?
Right. Open questions about symptoms and changes give you clues.

q.q: Why does the process say to test the simplest, most likely causes first?
o: They're quick, likely and low risk
Right. A loose cable is far more likely than a failed board.
Every SLA requires it
SLAs set times, not troubleshooting order.
Simple fixes never need documenting
Every fix gets documented.
Complex causes never happen on user devices
They do. They are just less likely, so they come later.

q.q: You are about to replace the RAM in a desktop. How do you protect the module from static?
o: Touch the gold contacts to check they're clean
Fingers add oil and static to the contacts.
Stand on carpet so you stay still
Carpet builds up static.
Wear rubber gloves and leave the PC plugged in
Gloves don't drain static, and a live PC is a shock risk.
Unplug it and wear an ESD wrist strap
Right. Unplug first. The strap then drains static so it can't zap the module, and you hold it by the edges.

q.q: A desktop's power supply smells burnt and you must open the case. What do you do first?
o: Shut down, unplug it and wait before opening
Right. Remove the power first, and give parts time to cool and discharge.
Open the case while it runs, to see what is burning
A live, damaged PSU is a shock and fire risk.
Spray the inside with a water-based cleaner
Water on live parts is dangerous.
Vacuum the dust out while it is on
Vacuums create static and the PC is still powered.

q.q: A laptop's battery has swollen and the case is bulging. What should you do?
o: Charge it overnight to see if it goes down
Charging a damaged battery raises the fire risk.
Stop using it and use the disposal process
Right. A swollen lithium battery can catch fire, so isolate it and dispose of it properly.
Throw it in the regular trash
Lithium batteries need proper recycling.
Press it flat so the case closes
Pressing a swollen cell can puncture it and start a fire.

q.q: You must lift a 25 kg printer from a cart onto a desk. Which is the safest method?
o: Drag it across the floor by its cable
You'd damage the cable and the printer.
Twist your body while lifting to place it
Twisting under a load causes injury.
Bend at the waist and lift quickly
That strains your back.
Bend your knees and get a second person
Right. Lift with your legs, and share the load.

q.q: Which TWO habits keep you safe while working inside a PC? (Choose two.)
o: Keep a drink next to the open case
A spill could cause a short.
Remove loose jewelry and tie back long hair
Right. Both can touch live parts or get caught in fans.
Work with the PSU cover open
Never open a power supply. It holds dangerous charge.
Unplug the power cord before opening the case
Right. This removes the main shock risk.
Leave tools and cables across the walkway
That is a trip hazard.

q.q: A user must tell you the host name and Windows version. Which tool shows both together?
o: The Task Manager Startup tab
It lists the apps that start with Windows.
Device Manager
It lists hardware and drivers.
System Information
Right. System Information lists the system name, OS version and hardware.
Event Viewer
It holds logs, not a summary.

q.q: A Mac user wants to read you the model, memory and macOS version quickly. Where do they look?
o: Apple menu > About This Mac
Right. It shows the chip, memory and macOS version on one screen.
AirDrop
It shares files. It doesn't show hardware details.
Activity Monitor
It shows live processes.
Console
It shows logs.

q.q: A user pastes this from a command prompt. Which value is the MAC address?
o: That is the default gateway.
LAPTOP-0427
That is the host name.
Right. 'Physical Address' is the MAC address, six pairs of hex digits.
That is the IPv4 address.
q.code:
C:\> ipconfig /all

   Host Name . . . . . . : LAPTOP-0427
   Physical Address. . . : 00-1A-2B-3C-4D-5E
   IPv4 Address. . . . . : 192.168.1.45
   Default Gateway . . . : 192.168.1.1

q.q: A user's PC restarted by itself overnight. Which Windows tool shows the errors from that time?
o: Device Manager
It shows device and driver status.
Event Viewer
Right. It keeps timestamped logs of system errors and events.
System Information
It shows the setup, not a history of events.
Task Manager
It shows what is running now, not the past.

q.q: A Mac feels slow. Which tool shows live CPU and memory use by app?
o: Activity Monitor
Right. It is the Mac's version of Task Manager.
Disk Utility
It checks and formats disks.
About This Mac
It shows the specs, not live use.
System Settings
It changes settings and doesn't show live use.

q.q: A meeting-room TV has HDMI. A user's thin laptop only has USB-C ports. What is the quickest fix?
o: A USB-C to HDMI adapter
Right. Many USB-C ports carry video, and an adapter completes the link if the port supports it.
A Micro USB charging cable
That only carries power and a little data.
An RJ-45 patch cable
That is for network links, not video.
A USB-A to HDMI cable
The laptop has no USB-A port, and USB-A can't carry video this way.

q.q: Which cable is shielded to help in places with a lot of electrical noise?
o: Shielded twisted pair (STP)
Right. The metal shield cuts interference.
Unshielded twisted pair (UTP)
UTP has no shield. It suits most offices.
A VGA cable
VGA carries analog video and is no network cable.
A power cord
A power cord carries no data.

q.q: Which connector do you find on a wired Ethernet cable?
o: DisplayPort
That is a video connector.
RJ-45
Right. RJ-45 is the standard Ethernet plug.
USB-B
That is a square USB plug used on printers.
VGA
That is an analog video connector.

q.q: An old projector only has a blue, 15-pin analog video port. What is it?
o: Thunderbolt
Thunderbolt uses a USB-C style plug.
HDMI
HDMI is digital and has a thin trapezoid plug.
VGA
Right. VGA is the blue 15-pin analog port.
DisplayPort
DisplayPort is digital and has a flat, notched plug.

q.q: A laptop's USB-C port has a small lightning-bolt symbol next to it. What does that usually mean?
o: It supports Thunderbolt
Right. Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use the USB-C shape, with fast data, video and power on one cable.
It is a serial port
Serial ports are old D-shaped connectors.
It only charges the battery
Thunderbolt carries much more than power.
It accepts only Ethernet
Ethernet uses RJ-45.

q.q: A user's PC boots from a slow hard disk. Which upgrade will make it feel fastest?
o: Add a second hard disk
More space doesn't make the boot drive faster.
Replace the drive with an SSD
Right. An SSD has no moving parts and loads the OS and apps much faster.
Add a sound card
That has no effect on boot speed.
Buy a bigger monitor
That has no effect on speed.

q.q: Which statement about an M.2 NVMe drive is true?
o: It needs both a SATA data cable and a power cable
A SATA drive does. An M.2 card sits on the board.
It is slower than a hard disk
It is far faster.
It plugs into the board and beats SATA speed
Right. No cables are needed, and NVMe uses fast PCIe lanes.
It only works in laptops
Many desktop boards have M.2 slots.

q.q: After a graphics card is installed, the screen is stuck at a low resolution and Device Manager lists 'Microsoft Basic Display Adapter'. What do you do?
o: Install the driver
Right. The basic adapter is Windows' stand-in until the real driver is installed.
Turn on BitLocker
BitLocker encrypts drives. It has nothing to do with this.
Reseat the RAM
RAM isn't the cause.
Replace the monitor
The monitor is fine. The driver is missing.

q.q: An old motherboard has failed and the shelf is full. Where should it go?
o: Into the regular trash
Electronics contain hazardous materials.
Back on the supply shelf, unmarked
Someone could install a bad part later.
To an approved e-waste recycler
Right. Boards hold materials that shouldn't go to a landfill.
Into a burn barrel
Burning electronics releases toxic fumes.

q.q: A desktop board has DDR5 memory slots. Which module can you install?
o: Any module that looks about right
Check the type the board supports first.
A laptop SO-DIMM, pushed in hard
It is a different size. Forcing it breaks things.
A DDR4 DIMM
It has a different notch and won't fit or work.
A DDR5 DIMM
Right. Memory generations aren't interchangeable.

q.q: A user's PC shows no lights and won't turn on. What do you check first?
o: Update the BIOS
The PC can't even start.
Reinstall Windows
The OS isn't the problem if nothing powers up.
Replace the motherboard
That is a costly last step.
Check the power cable
Right. Start with the simplest cause: is it plugged in and powered on?

q.q: A designer's 3D app needs 16 GB of RAM and a dedicated graphics card. The PC has 8 GB and integrated graphics, and the app crawls. What is the likely cause?
o: An expired certificate
That would show errors, not slowness.
A full browser cache
The app isn't a web page.
The PC doesn't meet the app's hardware requirements
Right. Always compare an app's requirements with the device.
A weak Wi-Fi signal
The app runs on the PC itself.

q.q: Device Manager shows a yellow warning triangle on the webcam. What does it mean?
o: The webcam is working and in use
A working device shows no warning.
The user turned the webcam off
A disabled device shows a down arrow instead.
A BIOS update is installing
A BIOS update doesn't show this way.
A device problem, often a driver
Right. Open its properties to read the error, then fix the driver.

q.q: What is one danger of a firmware update?
o: It always deletes the user's files
Firmware doesn't touch user files.
It extends the warranty
Updates don't change warranty terms.
A bad update can leave it unable to start
Right. Firmware runs before the OS, so a failed update can brick the device.
It can only be done by reinstalling the OS
Most updates run from a vendor tool.

q.q: A desktop gives a repeating beep pattern at power-on and won't start. What is the best next step?
o: Look up the board's beep codes
Right. Beep codes are a built-in status signal.
Ignore the beeps, they're normal
Repeating beeps signal a fault.
Reset the user's password
A hardware fault has nothing to do with passwords.
Replace the monitor
The beeps come from the PC, not the screen.

q.q: A user returns from vacation and can't sign in because the account is locked. What do you do?
o: Verify them, then unlock it
Right. Check who is asking, then unlock the account in the directory (such as Active Directory).
Replace the keyboard
A keyboard doesn't lock an account.
Delete the account and make a new one
That would lose their settings, group memberships and files access.
Reinstall the operating system
A locked account is a directory issue, not an OS fault.

q.q: A user got a new phone and can't approve sign-in prompts from their authenticator app. What is the best step?
o: Verify them, then re-register the app
Right. Verify identity first, then help them set up the authenticator again through the approved process.
Email them a one-time code with no checks
You haven't confirmed who is asking.
Have them borrow a coworker's phone
MFA devices belong to one person.
Turn MFA off for the account for good
That weakens the account for everyone who might attack it.

q.q: A user's S: drive shows a red X. Coworkers can still open it. What do you check first?
o: Reformat the file server
That would destroy everyone's data.
Check VPN and group membership
Right. Network reach and group membership are the usual causes of a drive that suddenly stops working.
Re-image every PC on the floor
Only one user is affected.
Replace the user's monitor
A display has no link to a drive mapping.

q.q: You added a user to a group that gets a mapped drive through Group Policy, but the drive hasn't appeared. Which command pulls the new policy now?
o: nslookup
That tests name lookups.
gpupdate /force
Right. It refreshes Group Policy without waiting for the next cycle.
ipconfig /renew
That renews the DHCP address lease.
netstat -an
That lists connections and ports.

q.q: A user can open a shared folder but gets 'Access denied' when saving a file in it. What is the likely cause?
o: They only have read access
Right. Reading works, but saving needs write permission.
Their MAC address changed
They're connected. This is a permission problem.
The folder is in a different time zone
Time zones don't control permissions.
DNS is down
They reached the folder, so names are resolving.

q.q: A company signs users in to its cloud apps with Microsoft Entra ID. What is Entra ID?
o: A DNS server program
DNS turns names into addresses.
A cloud-based identity service
Right. It's Microsoft's cloud identity and access management service.
A printer driver library
Drivers have nothing to do with sign-in.
A hypervisor for virtual machines
A hypervisor runs virtual machines.

q.q: A user's print job sits in the queue. The printer is on and shows Ready. What is the most direct fix?
o: Rename the printer
A new name won't clear a stuck job.
Replace the toner
Toner doesn't hold a job in the queue.
Update the monitor driver
The monitor isn't involved.
Clear the print queue
Right. A stuck job blocks the ones behind it. Clear the queue or restart the print spooler, then resend.

q.q: A laser printer leaves faded streaks on every page, and its toner is low. What do you do?
o: Replace the toner cartridge
Right. Low toner is the usual cause of faded streaks.
Clear the browser cache
A cache doesn't affect print quality.
Load the paper upside down
That won't fix toner streaks.
Reinstall the operating system
It's a printer supply problem.

q.q: Paper has jammed inside a printer. What is the safe way to clear it?
o: Spray lubricant on the rollers
Oil makes the paper slip and hurts print quality.
Yank it out from whichever side is easiest
Pulling the wrong way tears paper and bends parts.
Leave it and print again
That makes the jam worse.
Open the access panel and pull gently
Right. Gentle pulling with the feed direction avoids tearing and damage.

q.q: A Bluetooth headset connects, but the other people on a video call can't hear the user. What do you check first?
o: Replace the monitor
The screen isn't the issue.
Update the BIOS
The BIOS has no part in this.
Clear the browser cache
A cache doesn't control the microphone.
Choose it as the mic
Right. A headset can pair for audio out and still not be the selected input.

q.q: A wireless mouse is jumpy and sometimes freezes. What is the best first step?
o: Reinstall Windows
That is far too drastic.
Replace the motherboard
Overkill for a mouse.
Reset the user's password
Passwords don't affect a mouse.
Replace the batteries
Right. Weak batteries and distance are the usual causes.

q.q: A meeting-room touch panel doesn't react when touched. What is the most sensible first step?
o: Clean the screen, then restart the device
Right. Smudges and glitches are the common causes, and a restart is cheap.
Order a replacement right away
Try the simple steps before spending money.
Reset the network switch for the whole building
That would disrupt everybody.
Change the room's light bulbs
Light has no effect on a touch panel.

q.q: A user's PC shows this output. What does it tell you?
o: DHCP failed, so it self-assigned
Right. An address that starts 169.254 is self-assigned (APIPA), which means DHCP failed.
The PC has a valid address from the router
A router-assigned address would be in your normal range.
DNS is set up wrong
DNS is a separate setting.
The PC is using a public internet address
169.254.x.x isn't a public address.
q.code:
C:\> ipconfig

   IPv4 Address. . . . . : 169.254.13.88
   Subnet Mask . . . . . : 255.255.0.0
   Default Gateway . . . :

q.q: A user can ping 8.8.8.8 but web pages won't load by name. What is the most likely problem?
o: The default gateway is down
Pinging an outside address shows the gateway works.
DNS name lookups failing
Right. Reaching an IP address proves the link works, so names aren't resolving.
The PC has a self-assigned address
Then the ping would have failed too.
The network cable is cut
The ping got through.

q.q: A new laptop has IP 192.168.1.50, mask 255.255.255.0 and gateway 192.168.5.1. It can't leave its network. Why?
o: The mask is too long to use
A /24 mask is common and fine.
The address is a public one
192.168.x.x is private.
The gateway is in a different subnet, so the laptop can't reach it
Right. A gateway must sit in the same subnet as the host.
The laptop needs a bigger hard drive
Storage has no part in routing.

q.q: Which of these is a private IPv4 address?
o: That is a public DNS server.
172.32 is just outside the private range.
That is a public range.

q.q: A PC shows only an IPv6 address that starts fe80::. What does that tell you?
o: It has a link-local address only, and no global address has been assigned
Right. fe80:: is link-local, used on the local link.
It is an IPv4 address in short form
IPv4 and IPv6 are different formats.
It is a MAC address
A MAC address doesn't use colons in this form.
It has a public internet IPv6 address
A public address would not start fe80.

q.q: Two Wi-Fi names appear: 'CorpWiFi' and 'CorpWiFi-Guest'. An employee wants to use an internal printer. Which should they join?
o: Neither, a wired port is required
Wi-Fi to the corporate network is fine.
CorpWiFi, since guest is kept separate
Right. The SSID tells you which network you're on. Guest networks isolate users.
CorpWiFi-Guest, because it has the most users
Guest networks usually can't reach internal devices.
Either one, they always match
Different SSIDs can be different networks with different rules.

q.q: After a firewall rule change, an internal web app on port 8443 won't load, but other sites work. What is the likely cause?
o: The DHCP lease expired
Other sites would be down too.
The monitor is set to the wrong input
The display isn't related.
The firewall is blocking that port
Right. A firewall allows or blocks traffic by port and address.
The keyboard is faulty
A keyboard has no effect on one port.

q.q: Which command shows the path packets take to a host and where they stop?
o: traceroute
Right. traceroute (tracert on Windows) lists each hop, so you see where traffic dies.
nslookup
It looks up DNS records.
ipconfig /all
It shows your own settings.
gpupdate
It refreshes Group Policy.

q.q: Which Linux command lists open ports and active connections on a host?
o: traceroute
It maps the path to a host.
ip addr
It shows addresses, not connections.
nslookup
It tests name lookups.
ss (or netstat)
Right. Both show listening ports and connections.

q.q: A second monitor is plugged in but stays black. Where do you check in Windows?
o: Windows Update history
That lists installed updates.
The Display settings
Right. Windows must detect the screen and be told how to use it.
BitLocker settings
That controls drive encryption.
Power Options sleep timer
That sets when the screen turns off.

q.q: After a BIOS update a laptop asks for a 48-digit key before it will start Windows. What is it asking for?
o: The BitLocker recovery key
Right. BitLocker asks for it when the startup setup has changed. IT can look it up for the device or user.
The user's sign-in password
A password isn't 48 digits.
The Wi-Fi password
Wi-Fi isn't up before Windows starts.
The Windows product key
That activates Windows. It isn't used at startup.

q.q: A PC has said 'restart required to finish updates' for days, and the security tool reports it is out of date. What do you advise?
o: Turn updates off for good
Skipping updates leaves known holes open.
Restart to finish updates
Right. Many updates only complete after a restart.
Delete the update folder
That can break Windows.
Reinstall Windows
A restart is enough.

q.q: Windows won't load normally after a driver install. What do you try?
o: Delete the Windows folder
That destroys the OS.
Boot into Safe Mode
Right. Safe Mode starts with minimal drivers, so you can remove or roll back the new one.
Clear the browser cache
A browser cache doesn't affect booting.
Reset the router
The problem is on the PC.

q.q: A user's laptop was replaced, and Desktop and Documents backup was on in OneDrive. How do you get their files back?
o: Pull them from the printer's memory
Printers don't store user files.
Use Task Manager's history
Task Manager doesn't hold files.
Ask BitLocker to rebuild them
BitLocker only encrypts drives.
Sign in to OneDrive on the new PC
Right. Cloud backup keeps the files off the old device.

q.q: A user says a web page still shows old prices after the company updated it. What is a quick, safe fix?
o: Replace the network cable
The connection works. The page copy is old.
Delete the user's profile
That's far too much for a cached page.
Reinstall the browser's operating system
A browser doesn't have its own OS.
Clear the browser cache and reload the page
Right. A cached copy can be served after the real page has changed.

q.q: A Mac app can't record the screen during a call. Where do you check?
o: AirDrop visibility
AirDrop is for sharing files.
Time Machine settings
Time Machine handles backups.
Allow it under Screen Recording
Right. macOS makes you approve each app for the screen.
The Activity Monitor energy tab
It shows power use.

q.q: A USB drive is plugged into a Mac and doesn't appear on the desktop. Which tool shows whether the Mac sees it?
o: Mission Control
It arranges windows and spaces.
Disk Utility
Right. Disk Utility lists connected drives and can mount them.
Activity Monitor
It lists processes.
AirDrop
It shares files wirelessly.

q.q: A user can't see a coworker's Mac in AirDrop. What do you check?
o: The Time Machine backup disk
Backups don't affect AirDrop.
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth on
Right. AirDrop needs both radios on, and the Mac must be visible to Contacts Only or Everyone.
Safe Mode only
No need to boot differently.
The screen resolution
That doesn't affect sharing.

q.q: A Mac app freezes with a spinning wheel. Which tool lets you see it is not responding and quit it?
o: Time Machine
It restores from backups.
Console
It displays logs and doesn't end apps.
Activity Monitor, or Force Quit
Right. Both can end a stuck process.
Disk Utility
It repairs disks.

q.q: A user deleted a document by mistake an hour ago, and uses Time Machine on an external drive. What do you do?
o: Reinstall macOS
That's drastic and doesn't bring back the file.
Erase the Mac and start over
That would wipe more data.
Boot into Safe Mode
Safe Mode doesn't restore files.
Restore it in Time Machine
Right. Time Machine keeps older copies of files.

q.q: A user with low vision needs a Mac to read on-screen text aloud. Which feature is that?
o: Time Machine
It makes backups.
AirDrop
It shares files.
VoiceOver, in the Accessibility settings
Right. VoiceOver is the built-in screen reader.
Gatekeeper
It checks app safety.

q.q: A phone won't charge from a wall charger. What do you try first?
o: Try another cable and charger
Right. Cables and dirty ports are the usual cause.
Install a new keyboard app
A keyboard doesn't affect charging.
Leave airplane mode on forever
It doesn't relate to charging.
A factory reset right away
That wipes the phone and rarely helps here.

q.q: A new phone can't send work email because the account isn't set up. What is needed?
o: Update the camera app
The camera has no link to mail.
Turn on Bluetooth
Bluetooth doesn't carry email.
Jailbreak the phone
That breaks security and isn't needed.
Add the work account
Right. Mail needs the right account details or a profile from the company.

q.q: A user lost a company phone that holds work email. Which MDM action protects the data?
o: Remotely lock or wipe it
Right. MDM can lock or wipe a lost device.
Email the user their old password
That does nothing for the phone.
Wait a week and see if it turns up
Delay leaves data exposed.
Reset the user's monitor
A monitor isn't involved.

q.q: A phone shows full cellular bars but a work app won't load, while coworkers on Wi-Fi are fine. What do you try first?
o: Delete the user's account
That's way too much.
Update the printer firmware
A printer isn't involved.
Restart, then check settings
Right. Toggle airplane mode or restart, then check the cellular and VPN settings.
Replace the phone right away
Test cheap steps first.

q.q: A phone is slow and apps crash, and its storage is almost full. What should the technician suggest?
o: Keep it charged to 100% only
Charge level doesn't fix storage.
Root or jailbreak it
That removes protections.
Free up space and restart
Right. Full storage causes crashes.
Turn off all security updates
That leaves the phone open to attack.

q.q: Microsoft 365 is used by a company through a web browser, and the vendor runs everything behind it. Which cloud model is that?
o: On-premises hosting
On-premises means the company runs it in its own building.
Infrastructure as a service (IaaS)
IaaS rents servers and storage.
Platform as a service (PaaS)
PaaS rents a platform to build and run apps.
Software as a service (SaaS)
Right. SaaS means you use the finished app and the vendor runs it.

q.q: What does a hypervisor do?
o: It encrypts a laptop disk
BitLocker or similar does that.
It filters spam email
That's a mail filter's job.
It runs virtual machines
Right. It shares the host's hardware between VMs.
It assigns IP addresses
DHCP does that.

q.q: A SaaS app is down for everyone at the company. Who fixes it?
o: The vendor fixes it; you update users
Right. You can't fix the vendor's service. You can keep users informed.
The printer team
They don't own this service.
The user, by clearing their cache
A cache can't fix a vendor outage.
You, by reinstalling the app on every PC
The app is hosted by the vendor.

q.q: Which TWO are public cloud providers? (Choose two.)
o: Hyper-V
It's a hypervisor.
Google Cloud Platform (GCP)
Right. GCP is one of the big three.
Amazon Web Services (AWS)
Right. AWS is a major public cloud.
VNC
That's a remote desktop tool.
Active Directory
It's a directory service.

q.q: A team wants to rent virtual servers and manage the operating system themselves. Which model is that?
o: Infrastructure as a service (IaaS)
Right. With IaaS the provider supplies the hardware and the customer manages the OS and above.
Software as a service (SaaS)
SaaS gives you a finished app.
Platform as a service (PaaS)
PaaS hides the OS from you.
A private leased line
That is a network link.

q.q: A user asks you to install a free PDF tool from a pop-up ad. What do you do?
o: Install it on the server instead
That spreads the risk to more systems.
Install it, because it's free
Free tools from ads often hide malware.
Install it after turning off antivirus
Never disable security to install something.
Decline and offer an approved tool
Right. Only install approved software from trusted sources, such as the company's software catalog.

q.q: Why is installing an app from 'unknown sources' risky?
o: It is never possible to remove them
They can be removed. The risk is what they do first.
It voids the SLA
An SLA is a service contract.
It always makes the phone slower
It isn't about speed.
Apps outside the official store aren't checked and may carry malware
Right. Stores vet apps. Random downloads aren't vetted.

q.q: Outlook keeps asking for a password right after the user changed it. What is the likely cause?
o: The printer queue is full
Printers aren't involved.
The firewall has no ports
Then nothing would work.
Update the saved password
Right. Old saved passwords cause repeated prompts.
The monitor is too bright
Brightness has no link.

q.q: In a collaboration app, a user's microphone works in other apps but not in this one. What do you check first?
o: App audio settings
Right. The app may be using the wrong device or lack permission to use the microphone.
The printer driver
Printers aren't involved.
The BIOS version
It's an app setting, not a firmware issue.
The monitor cable
Video isn't audio.

q.q: A user can only open an Excel file read-only because a coworker has it open. What do you tell them?
o: Turn off the firewall
Firewalls don't lock files.
Delete the file and start over
That loses the work.
Wait for them to close it
Right. A file open for editing is locked to others.
Reinstall Office
The app works. The file is in use.

q.q: A user gets an email from an unknown sender: 'Your mailbox is full. Click here to keep your account.' What kind of threat is it?
o: A hardware fault
It's a message, not a device failure.
A software update notice
Real updates don't ask you to click an email link to keep your account.
Phishing
Right. It uses a fake urgent message to push you to click.
A DHCP error
DHCP hands out addresses.

q.q: After installing a free tool, a user's PC is slow and shows pop-ups. What are the best first steps?
o: Disconnect it and scan for malware
Right. Contain it, check it, and tell the security team.
Delete the Windows folder
That destroys the OS and doesn't remove the cause.
Share the tool with coworkers who also want it
That spreads the infection.
Keep working and ignore it
Malware spreads and steals data.

q.q: Which statement describes spoofing?
o: Encrypting files and asking for payment
That is ransomware.
Faking a trusted sender or address, such as the CEO's email
Right. Spoofing pretends to be someone or something you trust.
Guessing a password one try at a time
That is a brute-force attack.
Sending bulk adverts to many people
That is spam.

q.q: A user gets a sign-in alert from another country for their account, and they were not travelling. What do you do?
o: Reset the password and escalate
Right. Unrecognized sign-ins suggest someone else has the password. Review MFA too.
Tell the user to turn alerts off
That hides the warning.
Ignore it until there are three alerts
One alert is enough to act on.
Delete the user's mailbox
That destroys data and doesn't stop the attacker.

q.q: Which password advice should you give a user?
o: A long, unique passphrase for each account
Right. Length and uniqueness matter, and a manager makes it easy.
Use a birthday with an exclamation mark
Birthdays are easy to guess.
Use the same strong password everywhere
One leak would expose every account.
Use a short password and change it daily
Short passwords are easy to crack, and daily changes lead to sticky notes.

q.q: A user's files suddenly have odd extensions and a note demands payment. What do you do first?
o: Pay the demand quickly
Payment is a policy decision, and it funds attackers.
Forward the note to the whole company
That would cause panic and risk more infections.
Disconnect it and call security
Right. Contain it and let the security team lead.
Restart the PC and keep working
That could spread the damage.

q.q: A caller says he is the CFO, is in a rush, and demands a password reset without the usual checks. What do you do?
o: Reset it, because he's the CFO
Rank doesn't prove who is calling.
Reset it, then verify later
The damage is done by then.
Follow the verification procedure
Right. Attackers rely on urgency and rank. The process protects everyone.
Text the new password to the number that called you
You'd hand a password to an unverified person.

q.q: Which is the strongest sign that an email from 'IT Support' is phishing?
o: It is addressed to your name
Attackers can personalize mail too.
Urgency and a look-alike link
Right. Urgency and a look-alike link are classic signs.
It has the company's name in it
Attackers copy company names.
It was sent during working hours
The time of day proves nothing.

q.q: Why are help desk staff a prime target for social engineering?
o: They never use computers
They use them all day.
They are paid the most in the company
Pay isn't the reason.
They can reset passwords
Right. Attackers use that helpfulness to get access.
They don't have a manager
Everyone has a manager.

q.q: A stranger in a delivery uniform asks you to hold open a badge-controlled door. What do you do?
o: Politely direct them to reception or security to be let in
Right. Tailgating is a common way in. Let the process work.
Let them in and walk them to any floor
You'd be bypassing access control.
Hold the door, since they're wearing a uniform
Uniforms are easy to fake.
Give them your badge for a minute
Never share badges.

q.q: Which TWO are signs of a social engineering call? (Choose two.)
o: Pressure to act right now
Right. Urgency keeps you from thinking.
The caller waits while you verify them
Patience is a good sign.
A request to skip the normal verification steps
Right. Attackers want you to bypass the checks.
The caller asks to be added to the queue
That's an ordinary request.
The caller reads back their ticket number
That is normal for a real customer.

q.q: Which item is personally identifiable information (PII)?
o: The company's public phone number
That's public business information.
The office Wi-Fi network name
It names a network, not a person.
A printer's model number
It identifies a device, not a person.
A customer's name and SSN together
Right. Those two together identify a person.

q.q: A user wants to email a spreadsheet of employee SSNs to a personal account to work from home. What do you advise?
o: Don't. Use approved tools instead
Right. Sensitive data stays inside approved systems.
Go ahead, it's only one email
One email can leak thousands of records.
Send it as a screenshot
A screenshot still leaks the data.
Rename the file so no one notices
That's hiding it, not protecting it.

q.q: Which is an example of proprietary information?
o: A public press release
It is already public.
Source code the company owns
Right. Proprietary information is the company's own valuable work.
The cafeteria menu
It is not sensitive.
A public job posting
It is already public.

q.q: While fixing a laptop you see HR files open on the screen. What do you do?
o: Read through them, since you're there
Curiosity about private files can be a policy violation.
Tell coworkers what you saw
That spreads private information.
Copy them to your USB drive as a backup
That is a data leak.
Don't read or copy the files
Right. Respect confidentiality and keep to your task.

q.q: Why do companies have confidentiality policies?
o: To stop users from using computers
They guide use. They don't ban it.
To make work slower on purpose
Policies aren't meant to slow people down.
To protect private information
Right. Policies set rules for who can see and share data.
To avoid hiring more staff
Hiring isn't the goal.

q.q: A user is working from home, and an app has failed. Which tool lets you see and control their screen after they accept?
o: Disk Defragmenter
It tidies a drive.
Remote Assistance
Right. Remote Assistance (or a similar tool) shares the screen once the user agrees.
ping
It only tests whether a host replies.
tracert
It maps the path to a host.

q.q: What should you do before you start a remote session on a user's PC?
o: Nothing, since you're IT
Remote control needs consent.
Get the user's consent
Right. Consent and clear communication come first.
Ask for their password
Remote tools don't need their password.
Turn off their antivirus
Never weaken security for support.

q.q: Which TWO are remote support tools? (Choose two.)
o: TeamViewer
Right. It's a remote support and control tool.
DHCP
It hands out IP addresses.
Disk Management
It manages local drives.
DNS
It turns names into addresses.
Virtual Network Computing (VNC)
Right. VNC shares a desktop across the network.

q.q: Which Windows feature connects to the full desktop of another Windows PC?
o: Remote Desktop
Right. Remote Desktop gives you a session on the other PC.
Snipping Tool
It takes screenshots.
Event Viewer
It reads logs.
BitLocker
It encrypts drives.

q.q: You have finished a remote session. What is the right way to close it?
o: Ask the user to log you out tomorrow
Close it yourself now.
Delete the session log
Logs are evidence.
Leave it open in case you need it again
Open remote access is a security risk.
End it, close access, note it
Right. Close access and record what happened.

q.q: A technician pastes a customer's error log, with names and account numbers, into a public AI chatbot. What is the problem?
o: The log is too long to read
Length isn't the concern.
AI can't read logs
It can, but that's not the point.
It may expose private data
Right. Don't put private data into tools the company hasn't approved.
AI chatbots are always private
Public tools may store what you type.

q.q: An AI tool gives a confident fix that doesn't work. What does this show?
o: The user typed the question wrong
Don't assume it's the user's fault.
AI should replace the knowledge base
It doesn't replace verified documentation.
AI can be wrong, so check it
Right. Verify against trusted sources and test.
AI is always right if it sounds sure
Confidence is not accuracy.

q.q: Which is an example of predictive AI in IT support?
o: A tool that draws a picture from text
That is generative AI.
A search box that matches exact words
That isn't AI.
A chatbot that writes a new help article from a prompt
That is generative AI.
A model that flags tickets likely to miss their SLA, based on past data
Right. Predictive AI forecasts outcomes from past patterns.

q.q: A company app shows an odd error that only your company uses. Where do you look first for a known fix?
o: A guess from memory
A guess isn't documentation.
Ask the user to work it out
That's your job to help with.
The internal knowledge base
Right. Company-specific fixes are written down there.
A random forum post
Outsiders may not know your setup.

q.q: A forum post recommends a risky registry edit for a problem you are seeing. What do you do?
o: Apply it on the user's PC at once
Untested changes can break the PC.
Post the user's data to ask for more help
That leaks private data.
Check the source and test it safely
Right. Forums can help, but prefer vendor documentation and test fixes safely before using them.
Never use any forum
Forums can be useful once checked.

q.title: Match the ticket note to the step
q.scenario: Six notes from one ticket. Pick the step of the problem-solving process each note shows.

rows.req: The user says: the Wi-Fi drops in the meeting room.
rows.why: This writes the problem down in the user's own words.

rows.req: Two other people on the third floor have it too, since Monday's update.
rows.why: Asking who else is hit, and since when, is gathering detail.

rows.req: The new access point firmware is the likely cause.
rows.why: Picking the most likely cause from the facts.

rows.req: Rolled the access point back to the older firmware.
rows.why: Carrying out the plan is the change.

rows.req: Watched the room for an hour with no drops.
Recorded the cause, the rollback and the result in the ticket.
rows.why: Writing it down closes the loop.

q.title: Pick the port or cable
q.scenario: Four needs. Pick the connector for each. Two options are distractors.

items.text: A wired network jack in an office.
An old projector with a blue 15-pin analog port.
items.why: VGA is the blue analog connector.

items.text: One slim port for data, power and video on a thin laptop.
Digital video and sound to a TV.
items.why: HDMI carries both in one cable.

q.title: Read the address
q.scenario: Five addresses from a help desk ticket. Pick what each one is.

rows.why: 169.254.x.x means DHCP failed and the PC picked its own address.
It is outside every private range, so it counts as a public address.
fe80:: is an IPv6 link-local address.

q.title: Pick the command
q.scenario: Four jobs. Pick the command for each. Two options are distractors.

items.text: Check whether a name turns into the right IP address.
items.why: nslookup asks DNS for the answer.

items.text: Find where traffic stops between you and a website.
items.why: tracert lists every hop on the way.

items.text: See the PC's address, mask, gateway and DNS in one view.
Pull new Group Policy settings right now.

q.title: Pick the tool
q.scenario: Five problems. Pick the tool that helps the most.

rows.req: A Windows app is frozen and will not close.
rows.why: Task Manager can end the task.

rows.req: You need last night's crash errors on a Windows PC.
rows.why: Event Viewer keeps the log with timestamps.

rows.req: A Windows driver shows a yellow warning icon.
rows.why: Device Manager shows device and driver status.

rows.req: A Mac is slow and you need to see which app uses the CPU.
rows.why: Activity Monitor is the Mac's live process view.

rows.req: A Mac user deleted a file and has a backup disk.

q.title: Name the threat
q.scenario: Five events. Pick the threat each one shows. One option is a distractor.

items.text: Bulk junk email with adverts and no attack.
A fake bank email links to a look-alike login page.
items.why: Phishing tricks you into entering your login.

items.text: A program encrypts files and demands payment.
items.why: Ransomware is a kind of malware.

items.text: A caller presses the help desk to reset a VP's password with no ID check.
items.why: Pressure and impersonation is social engineering.

items.text: Many failed sign-ins, then a success from an unknown country.
items.why: Someone got in who shouldn't have.
